headline: Eight Felda deals were audited in 2019. MACC opened papers on seven of them in 2026.
context: In 2019 the Economic Affairs Ministry had Ernst & Young audit eight Felda and FIC purchases and laid the findings before Parliament. A different government is now weighing a second audit, and the anti-graft agency has opened papers on seven of the same deals.

cards.big: Putrajaya is weighing whether to order a forensic audit of Felda. Ernst & Young delivered one in 2019, and Parliament has had it since.
cards.sub: It covered eight Felda and FIC purchases and was annexed to the FELDA White Paper, Command Paper 6 of 2019.

cards.big: Mohd Isa Abdul Samad's conviction became final on 26 June 2026, nearly nine years after MACC opened its first Felda hotel files in 2017.
cards.sub: Felda also sued 21 defendants for RM2 billion over the Jalan Semarak land in 2019. It was still in pretrial applications in 2025.

cards.big: Ernst & Young found RM4.38 billion committed across the eight deals. Roughly half of it, about RM2.2 billion, was already written off.
cards.sub: The auditors also found governance failure, approvals without due diligence, and elements of non-compliance and misconduct.

cards.big: MACC's seven Felda files, announced on 2 September 2026, cover seven of the eight deals Ernst & Young audited.
cards.sub: Only the Indonesian plantation stake is missing. MACC began probing the Kensington purchase in 2017 and says that file is still open.

cards.big: Seven of the eight deals were audited in 2019 and investigated in 2026. The seven years in between are the finding nobody commissioned.
Malaysia audited Felda more closely than almost any agency it owns. Scrutiny was never what failed. Follow-through was.
cards.sub: While the deals were being written down, the White Paper recorded settlers waiting on delayed Sara Hidup and Pendahuluan Hasil payments.
